edges.claim_a: There are 25,000 times more hours of content produced annually on YouTube than on traditional television networks and streaming services combined, yet digital media generates a smaller share of revenue and profit compared with its share of consumption.
edges.claim_b: Chinese exporters cut prices by an average of 8 percent to find buyers in new markets as US–China bilateral trade fell by approximately 30 percent due to tariffs.
edges.explanation: Across genuinely different disciplines, near-infinite supply collapses per-unit economics while the scarce complement (focused, high-intent attention in media; geopolitically trusted trade partnerships in global commerce) captures disproportionate value — a structural prediction that neither article makes alone but both independently instantiate: abundance destroys unit economics, and the scarce, high-trust complement becomes the true value driver.

edges.claim_a: 61% of respondents report negative tariff impacts on their costs, yet 71% of leaders are optimistic about their own company's performance in 2026
edges.claim_b: The United States replaced about two-thirds of the tariff-induced import gap with goods from other sellers, while trade grew faster than global output in 2025 despite dire predictions of retrenchment
edges.explanation: Both claims independently demonstrate that tariff-induced disruption failed to produce the aggregate contraction it predicted: at the firm level, cost pain coexists with sustained performance optimism, and at the macro trade level, import displacement coexisted with accelerating trade volume — the same non-obvious finding that tariff shocks redistribute rather than contract economic activity, appearing independently at micro and macro scales.
